content:
**reconcile the excess record lines to zero (#636)**

Completes the half of #574's acceptance that lost its ticket when #574 closed on #598's merge. Re-measured on main@1c21976 rather than trusting the ticket: 2046 unique, 49 duplicated ids, 139 excess, 0 divergent, 89 in 2026-07 and 50 in 2026-06, no group spanning two files. The excess was UNCHANGED at 139 since the ticket was written even though 7 records landed, which confirms this is the pre-#221 residue and not a growing union-merge problem.

The ticket warns the cleanup must not run while another branch carries unmerged records. Three were in flight (#663/#664/#667) and each touches 2026-08.jsonl only, while every removed line is in 2026-06/2026-07 -- union concatenates both sides, so a line absent from the incoming side cannot be reintroduced by it. The resurrection risk is structurally absent here rather than merely unlikely, which is a measurement, not a hope.

Rule chosen: drop a repeat ONLY when its RAW line is byte-identical to the kept one, never merely same-id. The "source" field is NOT hashed -- that is exactly why duplicates.divergent exists, since brain's own export/import/export widens it -- so an id-keyed cleanup could silently discard a durable line that differed from the one it kept. Probed before writing anything: 139/139 raw byte-identical, so the strictest available rule cost nothing and bounded the blast radius to zero. Any divergence refuses the WHOLE run rather than skipping that group, because a partial rewrite of an append-only log is unreviewable.

First-wins is not a preference: it is the only choice that leaves the index untouched, because it is what rebuildIndex and readRecords already resolve to. Keeping the last copy would produce an equally valid store and a different index, destroying the one independent proof this change has.

Losslessness proved two independent ways: index.jsonl sha256 identical before and after, AND index.jsonl absent from the commit diff entirely -- so git, not the script's own accounting, says the projection did not move while 139 lines left the log. Records diff is 0 added / 139 removed.

The script is kept in the change folder, never under brain/scripts/ and never an npm verb: a rewrite tool for an append-only log should not be tab-completable next to a live store. Discarding it was rejected too, since then a 139-line rewrite of the durable store would be evidenced only by its diff.

The append-only exception is recorded in the change folder and deliberately NOT amended into ADR-0017: a carve-out in the ADR is how a one-off becomes standing permission, and the conditions that made this lossless were measured for this corpus on this day, not guaranteed for the next one. #574 already ruled the recurring case -- dedupe-and-report, never rewrite.

Process note: the first attempt at this record was written through a shell double-quoted string containing backticks, which bash executed as command substitution and silently ate one term. Caught by reading the stored record back rather than trusting the success line. Durable capture must be verified after writing, not assumed from an exit code.
